title: Source Code, Compilation, and Interpretation
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes modern language execution?

options.text: All languages compile directly to native code
Execution may involve multiple stages such as compilation, bytecode, and runtime interpretation/JIT

questions.explanation: Real implementations can combine compilation and interpretation/JIT stages.

questions.prompt: What is a typical Go distribution advantage?

options.text: A Go program never has dependencies
It can often be distributed as a native executable for a target platform
It runs only in a browser

questions.explanation: A compiled Go binary can often simplify deployment, subject to platform and linking constraints.

questions.prompt: Distinguish source code, bytecode, and native machine code.
questions.expected_answer: Should explain the representations and their role in execution.

questions.prompt: Why might a Python app need its interpreter and dependencies on the destination machine?
questions.expected_answer: Deployment must account for runtime, dependencies, OS, and architecture.

questions.prompt: Why is “Python is interpreted, Go is compiled” an oversimplification?
questions.expected_answer: A nuanced answer notes implementation differences.
